title: Incentive Complexity, Bounded Rationality, and Effort Provision
story_ladder: standard contract theory assumes workers see all incentives clearly -> real incentive systems are complex -> complexity creates opacity -> opacity changes effort, efficiency, and welfare
framework: theoretical framework -> field experiments in the warehouse -> transparent benchmark comparison -> robustness and equilibrium welfare -> online experiments and mechanism tests
innovation_source: the paper's innovation is to turn complexity from a nuisance into the main causal object and to link it to measurable cognitive heterogeneity in labor-contract response
reusable_move: if a standard model assumes away an informational or cognitive friction, isolate that friction directly and make it the contribution rather than only a caveat

title: Drivers of Change: Employment Responses to the Lifting of the Saudi Female Driving Ban
story_ladder: landmark rights reform should improve labor outcomes -> de jure reform alone is hard to identify -> randomize de facto access -> find both economic gains and household backlash
framework: institutional setting -> experimental design -> estimation strategy -> individual driving and employment responses -> intrahousehold responses -> heterogeneity
innovation_source: the paper uses rationed postreform access to identify a major legal change and then broadens the outcome space beyond employment to include agency and household bargaining
reusable_move: when a legal reform is universal, look for a rationed implementation margin that creates experimental or quasi-experimental access to the new right

title: From Retributive to Restorative: An Alternative Approach to Justice in Schools
story_ladder: schools fear that less harsh discipline may reduce safety and learning -> evaluate a restorative alternative -> punitive outcomes fall while academic averages do not deteriorate -> justice reform looks less costly than critics assume
framework: conceptual framework -> policy setting and rollout -> data and sample -> empirical strategy -> main results -> disruption mechanisms -> heterogeneity
innovation_source: the innovation is to reframe school-discipline policy as an institutional justice design problem and to test both punishment and spillover-to-classroom concerns together
reusable_move: when a reform is criticized on spillover grounds, put the feared spillover outcome directly next to the target outcome so the paper can adjudicate the full trade-off

title: Gender-Biased Technological Change: Milking Machines and the Exodus of Women from Farming
story_ladder: automation is often studied as skill-biased or routine-biased -> here the key bias is gendered task replacement -> displacement from agriculture leads to upward movement elsewhere
framework: historical background -> data construction -> research design -> short-run migration and employment effects -> longer-run education and earnings consequences
innovation_source: the contribution is to identify a technology whose task incidence is distinctly gendered and to trace its long-run effects well beyond immediate displacement
reusable_move: to make technology papers sharper, look for task-level incidence that maps cleanly onto a demographic group rather than only onto a skill bucket

title: Just a Few Seeds More: The Value of Network Data for Diffusion
story_ladder: network science says better targeting should matter -> benchmark that value against a simpler policy margin -> find that more data often buys surprisingly little
framework: model and main theorem -> network-class illustrations -> extensions to homophily and real networks -> policy interpretation of the value of data
innovation_source: the innovation is to shift the question from how to target optimally to whether fine targeting is worth the information cost at all
reusable_move: before optimizing a sophisticated policy object, compare it to a dumb but scalable substitute; the innovation may come from bounding the value of sophistication

title: Monetary Policy and Rational Asset Price Bubbles: Comment
story_ladder: prior result seems to imply policy impotence or perversity -> isolate the exact object of the claim -> show impact stabilization remains possible under aggressive action
framework: revisit the original model -> build a closed-form alternative -> add monetary policy -> reinterpret the scope of the earlier paradox
innovation_source: the paper's contribution is clarificatory rather than expansive: it disentangles different meanings of "can policy dampen bubbles?"
reusable_move: in a comment-style paper, redefine the claim precisely and then show that the earlier result answered a narrower question than readers thought

title: Consistent Evidence on Duration Dependence of Price Changes
story_ladder: price-setting evidence depends on difficult hazard estimation -> build a cleaner estimator -> show the empirical picture of duration dependence and macro implications changes
framework: related literature and model -> identification and censoring issues -> estimator development -> application to price spells -> macro interpretation
innovation_source: the main innovation is methodological, but it is made consequential by linking estimation consistency directly to a substantive macro question
reusable_move: a methods paper becomes stronger when the empirical application visibly overturns or sharpens an important substantive debate

title: Spillovers in State Capacity Building: Evidence from the Digitization of Land Records in Pakistan
story_ladder: digitization is usually sold as state-capacity improvement -> reform indeed modernizes one domain -> bureaucratic reorganization spills over negatively to another -> state capacity is not modular
framework: background and data -> effect on tax collection -> decomposition into tax base versus bureaucrat performance -> bureaucratic-organization mechanisms -> implications for state-capacity design
innovation_source: the contribution is to show that technological state-building can have cross-task spillovers through bureaucratic organization, not just direct productivity effects
reusable_move: when studying capacity reforms, always ask what complementary informal or multitask arrangements the reform destroys, not only what formal process it upgrades

title: Labor Market Power, Self-Employment, and Development
story_ladder: self-employment is often treated as a symptom of underdevelopment -> reframe it as both symptom and countervailing force -> policy that reduces it may have ambiguous welfare consequences
framework: data and descriptive facts -> estimation of labor market power -> structural model -> counterfactual industrial-policy experiments -> development interpretation
innovation_source: the paper's innovation is to treat self-employment as an equilibrium outside option within an oligopsony framework rather than as a passive residual sector
reusable_move: if a large informal or residual sector exists, ask whether it is also disciplining a formal market imperfection; that reversal often creates a publishable angle

title: Borrowing and Spending in the Money: Debt Substitution and the Cash-Out Refinance Channel of Monetary Policy
story_ladder: conventional wisdom says in-the-money refinancing drives spending transmission -> rate shocks kill cash-outs -> substitution offsets much of the decline -> the refinance channel is weaker and less path dependent than advertised
framework: data and stylized patterns -> conceptual framework -> rate-gap identification -> extensive and intensive borrowing responses -> substitution with other debt -> robustness
innovation_source: the contribution is to reinterpret an iconic monetary-policy channel by moving from one borrowing product to the household balance sheet as the true object
reusable_move: if a policy channel is inferred from one salient product margin, rebuild the analysis around the broader balance-sheet object before drawing macro conclusions

title: The End of Privilege: A Reexamination of the Net Foreign Asset Position of the United States
story_ladder: the United States was thought to enjoy favorable valuation reappraisals -> post-2007 data show the opposite -> model-based accounting reveals a reversal of privilege rooted in corporate equity valuations
framework: recent evolution of the current account and NFA -> model -> measurement strategy -> baseline decomposition -> counterfactuals and welfare interpretation
innovation_source: the paper combines updated external-balance accounting with a model that embeds realistic asset valuations, allowing it to reinterpret a famous macrofinance fact
reusable_move: revisit canonical country-level narratives when new balance-sheet composition changes the welfare meaning of familiar aggregates

title: Robust Misspecified Models
story_ladder: economists often assume false models lose out with enough data -> show that model competition with sticky switching allows false models to survive indefinitely -> clarify why entrenched simple models persist
framework: motivating example -> general framework -> main robustness results -> applications to media bias and polarization and related settings
innovation_source: the innovation is to formalize the persistence of misspecified models in a competitive-learning environment rather than treating misspecification as a static estimation flaw
reusable_move: when a field puzzle concerns persistence of bad beliefs or bad models, write down the comparison process itself; persistence often comes from the switching environment, not just from the belief content

title: Quid Pro Quo, Knowledge Spillovers, and Industrial Quality Upgrading: Evidence from the Chinese Auto Industry
story_ladder: policy debate asks whether forced technology transfer ever works -> move from output quantity to multidimensional quality -> show affiliated domestic firms upgrade in the specific dimensions where partners excel
framework: background on quid pro quo and industry evolution -> quality-upgrading evidence -> identification using within-product quality structure -> mechanisms through workers and suppliers
innovation_source: the contribution is to study spillovers via rich product-quality dimensions rather than crude productivity proxies, making imitation and upgrading directly visible
reusable_move: when spillovers are hard to detect in aggregate outcomes, move to the specific attributes where the source firm has comparative strength

title: Increasing Degree Attainment among Low-Income Students: The Role of Intensive Advising and College Quality
story_ladder: low-income students underattain degrees -> advising could matter through many channels -> RCT shows large gains -> quality of initial college match emerges as the main engine
framework: program background -> experimental design and data -> strategy and main results -> heterogeneity and mechanism via college quality
innovation_source: the paper's innovation is to connect advising effects to college quality and to use preadvising preferences to show the channel more directly
reusable_move: if an intervention improves a long-run outcome, identify whether it changed the quality of the initial match or the productivity within the match; that distinction sharpens the contribution

title: Similarity of Information and Collective Action
story_ladder: common intuition says shared information should aid coordination -> collective action also has free-riding -> theory shows the sign is state dependent -> explains mixed evidence in protests and group decision-making
framework: baseline regime-change game -> information-similarity order -> equilibrium participation results -> welfare -> applications to protests, committees, and public goods
innovation_source: the innovation is to formulate a general order of information similarity and show that the same informational change can flip sign across environments
reusable_move: when literatures report opposing empirical patterns, search for a state variable that makes both patterns consistent inside one framework

title: Distinguishing Causes of Neighborhood Racial Change: A Nearest-Neighbor Design
story_ladder: neighborhood racial change has many overlapping causes -> isolate the most local interpersonal margin -> show direct neighbor identity matters -> clarify how much can and cannot be attributed to that mechanism
framework: conceptual framework -> nearest-neighbor research design -> data implementation -> main estimates -> interpretation relative to broader neighborhood-change narratives
innovation_source: the contribution is the extremely local design that strips away much of the usual confounding in studies of racial neighborhood transition
reusable_move: when a classic question suffers from too many bundled mechanisms, build a design that isolates the smallest feasible unit where one mechanism should operate

title: “Potential” and the Gender Promotion Gap
story_ladder: promotion gaps are often examined through observed performance -> firms say they promote on future potential -> data show potential ratings are biased and consequential -> subjective forecasting category becomes the wedge
framework: background on nine-box evaluations -> setting and data -> promotion regressions -> validation against future performance -> robustness and implications
innovation_source: the paper's innovation is to identify "potential" as a distinct evaluative object that mediates inequality above and beyond current performance
reusable_move: if an organization explicitly uses a soft internal category, study that category directly instead of proxying it with standard outcomes

title: Real Credit Cycles
story_ladder: financial instability is often attributed to large exogenous financial shocks -> build a model where beliefs create endogenous fragility -> match credit-cycle facts with smaller shocks
framework: data diagnostics -> diagnostic-expectations mechanism -> quantitative model -> cycle implications and empirical fit
innovation_source: the contribution is to make expectations distortions quantitatively central in a workhorse credit model rather than leaving them as an auxiliary behavioral add-on
reusable_move: to revive a behavioral mechanism in macro, show it can match first-order aggregate facts with realistic parameter magnitudes

title: Nonlinear Pricing and Misallocation
story_ladder: standard misallocation logic treats markup dispersion as the key signal -> introduce realistic nonlinear pricing -> the interpretation of observed markups flips -> new misallocation margin emerges
framework: model environment -> efficient versus market allocation -> sources of distortion -> aggregate implications -> empirical prevalence and quantification in retail data
innovation_source: the paper's innovation is to challenge a dominant diagnostic metric in macro IO by altering the pricing environment to match actual contracts
reusable_move: if a literature relies on a simple diagnostic statistic, ask whether that statistic survives under a more realistic contract form; overturning the diagnostic can be the contribution

title: Changing Income Risk across the US Skill Distribution: Evidence from a Generalized Kalman Filter
story_ladder: overall earnings volatility can hide very different underlying risks -> build a method to decompose them for every worker-period -> show persistent risk rises in high-skill, tech-exposed jobs
framework: theoretical motivation -> econometric framework -> data -> time trends in risk -> heterogeneity by skill and occupation -> technology-adoption mechanism
innovation_source: the contribution is dual: a tractable estimation framework for income dynamics and a new substantive account of rising risk among high-skill workers
reusable_move: methods papers land better when the new tool answers a "for whom and why" question that older aggregate decompositions could not resolve

title: Take the Goods and Run: Contracting Frictions and Market Power in Supply Chains
story_ladder: weak enforcement is usually treated as purely harmful -> market power is also present in these environments -> the two distortions interact in a second-best way -> fixing only one friction can backfire
framework: context and data -> motivating facts -> empirical dynamic contracting model -> estimation -> counterfactual institutional reforms
innovation_source: the paper turns a standard development frictions question into a second-best interaction problem and measures the efficiency path of relationships over time rather than only their average level
reusable_move: when two distortions plausibly offset each other, do not study either in isolation; the contribution can come from showing that unilateral reform is not the right benchmark

title: The Debt-Inflation Channel of the German (Hyper)Inflation
story_ladder: inflation transmission is often discussed through price rigidities -> an extreme historical episode isolates the balance-sheet channel -> highly levered firms expand relative to others -> debt contracts are themselves a nominal rigidity
framework: conceptual framework -> historical and firm-level data -> aggregate evidence -> cross-firm leverage design -> interpretation and external-validity discussion
innovation_source: the contribution is to use a famous macro episode not to restudy its causes but to identify a specific transmission channel with firm-level heterogeneity
reusable_move: when a historical event is canonical, reopen it with a sharper channel question and a newly digitized micro dataset rather than retelling the familiar aggregate narrative

title: Gender Differences in Financial Advice
story_ladder: advice should help less sophisticated investors the most -> advisor incentives are not aligned with client welfare -> the vulnerable group becomes the more exploitable group -> advice can widen, not close, financial inequality
framework: data construction -> evidence on gender gaps in recommendations and prices -> implementation behavior -> mechanism evidence from client and advisor beliefs
innovation_source: the paper ties observed recommendations to beliefs about clients and to advisor-side heterogeneity, allowing a much cleaner mechanism story than administrative data alone would permit
reusable_move: if a paper studies discrimination in a complex market, combine action data with elicited beliefs so the mechanism is not left as a vague residual

title: The Value of Clean Water: Experimental Evidence from Rural India
story_ladder: piped water is expensive and chlorine is unpopular -> test a different production and distribution bundle -> households reveal much higher valuation than the literature implied -> the welfare case for clean-water access strengthens
framework: background -> experiment design -> demand and valuation results -> health outcomes -> cost-effectiveness and policy interpretation
innovation_source: the paper directly experimentally recovers both willingness to pay and willingness to accept for clean water rather than inferring value from adoption of weaker products
reusable_move: when earlier demand estimates seem too small, ask whether the literature has been estimating valuation for a bundled inconvenience rather than for the core good itself

title: When Product Markets Become Collective Traps: The Case of Social Media
story_ladder: market demand and surplus are usually evaluated holding aggregate use fixed -> network goods change the value of opting out -> a popular product can become a collective trap -> standard welfare accounting breaks
framework: conceptual framework -> measurement design -> social-media application -> heterogeneity in product-market valuation
innovation_source: the paper reframes consumer welfare from an individual fixed-environment object into an equilibrium object that embeds the value of not participating
reusable_move: if the good changes the quality of nonconsumption, the standard welfare object is probably wrong; redefine the object before arguing about magnitudes

title: Dynamics of the Long-Term Housing Yield: Evidence from Natural Experiments
story_ladder: housing valuations are central but long-run yield is hidden -> lease extensions create repeated pricing experiments -> a real-time series of the latent yield can be recovered -> the long-run discount environment has shifted sharply
framework: conceptual object -> institutional setting and data -> estimator -> time-series results -> cross-market heterogeneity and interpretation
innovation_source: the paper finds a specific transaction margin that prices a latent object of macro-finance interest and then turns it into a public measurement series
reusable_move: if a core equilibrium object is unobservable, search for a niche institutional margin that prices just that component and build the paper around it

title: Apart but Connected: Online Tutoring, Cognitive Outcomes, and Soft Skills
story_ladder: pandemic school closures generated severe inequality and isolation -> online tutoring looks like an imperfect substitute -> a randomized design shows meaningful academic gains and context-dependent soft-skill gains -> remote support is more powerful than expected
framework: intervention and design -> academic effects -> mechanism and heterogeneity -> tutor-side effects
innovation_source: the contribution is not just that tutoring works, but that a low-cost volunteer and fully online version can move both student outcomes and tutor attitudes
reusable_move: in education papers, measure effects on the provider side as well as the recipient side when the intervention itself is relational

title: Competition under Incomplete Contracts and the Design of Procurement Policies
story_ladder: procurement reform often treats more competition as unambiguously good -> incomplete contracts mean award price is not the whole object -> cheaper winners can perform worse -> optimal procurement policy must internalize post-award execution
framework: setting and institutional threshold -> reduced-form evidence on price and nonprice outcomes -> structural auction model -> counterfactual policy design
innovation_source: the paper pairs a clean quasi-experiment with a model that makes the price-performance trade-off structurally explicit
reusable_move: when a policy improves the visible metric, put the hidden but policy-relevant downstream metric right next to it; that contrast can carry the paper

title: First-Generation Elite: The Role of School Social Networks
story_ladder: Norway has free tuition and centralized admissions yet still shows strong elite persistence -> missing ingredient is social capital -> peer exposure changes both learning and application behavior -> the design of grading and school mixing shapes mobility
framework: institutional background -> peer-effect design -> GPA channel decomposition -> mediation through application behavior -> long-run earnings and mobility simulations
innovation_source: the paper turns peer exposure into a social-capital mechanism for elite persistence and uses an exam lottery to identify the mediator rather than stopping at reduced-form peer effects
reusable_move: when a treatment works through a contested mediator, look for an institutional lottery or rule that generates exogenous movement in the mediator itself

title: Sequential Learning under Informational Ambiguity
story_ladder: Bayesian social learning gives fragile cascade predictions -> real agents are also unsure how informative others are -> ambiguity is introduced -> cascades become the robust outcome rather than the exception
framework: model -> equilibrium and learning concepts -> main results under bounded and unbounded signals -> comparison with alternative ambiguity preferences
innovation_source: the paper recasts a classic learning result by moving uncertainty one layer up, from signals themselves to the data-generating process behind observed actions
reusable_move: when a canonical theoretical result is known to be fragile, ask whether adding one realistic meta-uncertainty makes a qualitatively different outcome robust

title: The Opportunity Atlas: Mapping the Childhood Roots of Social Mobility
story_ladder: place effects matter but existing evidence is too coarse for targeting -> build a tract-level outcome atlas -> show that standard proxies miss much of the variation -> create a policy and research tool grounded in actual long-run outcomes
framework: data -> tract-level estimation methodology -> descriptive and targeting results -> evidence on causal content -> applications
innovation_source: the contribution is equal parts measurement infrastructure and substantive economics: the dataset itself is the method, result, and policy object
reusable_move: a data paper becomes a top-field paper when it is framed around a decision problem that existing measures cannot solve

title: Zero-Sum Thinking and the Roots of US Political Differences
story_ladder: many US political preferences appear ideologically inconsistent -> a deeper mental model may reconcile them -> directly measure zero-sum thinking -> trace it to lived and inherited experience
framework: survey design and measurement -> political correlates -> historical predictors -> broader interpretation of US politics
innovation_source: the paper shifts from analyzing isolated policy attitudes to measuring a common underlying worldview and then connecting that worldview to historical lineage
reusable_move: when preferences look contradictory on the surface, search for the latent worldview that jointly rationalizes them and make that hidden construct the centerpiece

title: Tying with Network Effects
story_ladder: standard leverage theories of tying are contested -> network effects create a new strategic force -> tying becomes a best response without special commitment assumptions -> antitrust concerns survive in a different form
framework: illustrative example -> general model -> equilibrium analysis -> welfare implications
innovation_source: the paper identifies a leverage mechanism specific to network industries and thereby reopens an antitrust question that simpler models had narrowed
reusable_move: when an old debate seems settled, transplant it into a market environment with a qualitatively different force and ask whether the classic logic reappears

title: Default Options and Retirement Saving Dynamics
story_ladder: defaults look powerful in behavioral finance -> most evidence is short-run -> a dynamic perspective shows attenuation and heterogeneity -> long-run policy evaluation differs from the immediate response
framework: data and identification -> seven empirical facts -> dynamic model -> long-run policy implications
innovation_source: the paper's innovation is to make the behavioral phenomenon dynamic and distributional rather than treating the enrollment response as the whole object of interest
reusable_move: if a behavioral effect is famous because it is immediate, ask whether it survives when agents can later undo or compensate for it

title: An Equilibrium Analysis of the Effects of Neighborhood-Based Interventions on Children
story_ladder: reduced-form place studies identify local effects -> policy at scale changes equilibrium -> build a model where children, neighborhoods, and housing markets coevolve -> compare people-based and place-based interventions under general equilibrium
framework: motivating facts -> model -> estimation -> baseline counterfactuals -> policy comparison across city environments
innovation_source: the contribution is to place child-development neighborhood effects inside a citywide equilibrium system rather than treating neighborhoods as fixed containers
reusable_move: when two policy families are usually compared narratively, put them inside one equilibrium model and let city constraints determine where each wins

title: Monetary Policy and the Labor Market: A Quasi-experiment in Sweden
story_ladder: clean modern monetary case studies are rare -> the Swedish tightening looks unusually identifiable because it was driven by financial-stability concerns -> careful validation shows a large contraction -> the labor-market costs were both sizable and unequal
framework: methodology and identification case -> institutional narrative -> aggregate effects -> firm and worker heterogeneity -> distributional interpretation
innovation_source: the paper revives the case-study tradition but arms it with modern placebo logic and rich administrative microdata
reusable_move: one unusually clean episode can support a strong paper if the identification section systematically disproves the obvious confounders instead of merely asserting them away

title: Sequential Cursed Equilibrium
story_ladder: cursed equilibrium works in simultaneous settings but misfires in extensive games -> identify the psychological asymmetry between hypothetical and observed information -> build a new solution concept around that asymmetry -> recover more plausible dynamic predictions
framework: definitions and general results -> experimental evidence -> application to dynamic auctions -> discussion of limits and comparisons
innovation_source: the key innovation is not more behavioral noise but a precise redefinition of where strategic inference fails
reusable_move: strong behavioral theory papers often come from one carefully isolated cognitive asymmetry that can be formalized cleanly and shown to matter across multiple games

title: Politics at Work
story_ladder: politics is usually studied in explicitly political arenas -> partisan identity can also spill into private employment relationships -> rich microdata reveal strong assortative matching -> politics becomes an economic sorting force
framework: institutional context -> data construction -> assortative-matching measurement -> mechanism tests -> experimental evidence
innovation_source: the paper treats partisanship as a labor-market characteristic and combines multiple empirical lenses to separate network overlap from direct discrimination
reusable_move: if an identity variable matters outside its obvious domain, the paper gets sharper when it shows both matching patterns and within-firm consequences

title: Black Lives: The High Cost of Segregation
story_ladder: segregation is often discussed as a residential or distributional fact -> its most severe cost may be violent mortality -> a historical spatial design links segregation to homicide through the fiscal state
framework: data -> methodology -> homicide and crime results -> local-finance channel -> interpretation
innovation_source: the contribution is to connect segregation to an especially high-stakes outcome and to show that public-finance depletion is part of the causal chain
reusable_move: a paper can gain force by tracing a broad structural institution to a concrete life-and-death outcome through a measurable fiscal mechanism

title: Why Is Workplace Sexual Harassment Underreported? The Value of Outside Options amid the Threat of Retaliation
story_ladder: formal charges are not the same as true prevalence -> economic vulnerability changes the reporting decision -> shocks to outside options reveal the hidden reporting margin -> labor-market conditions shape measured harassment
framework: reported versus unreported harassment -> institutional background -> data -> shock-based selectivity tests -> interpretation and policy implications
innovation_source: the paper infers hidden underreporting from selection patterns in formal complaints and from divergence between formal and anonymous behavior
reusable_move: when the true outcome is unobserved, study the reporting technology itself and look for shocks that move reporting incentives without mechanically changing the underlying event

title: Negative Control Falsification Tests for Instrumental Variable Designs
story_ladder: placebo tests are widespread and treated as routine credibility checks -> the logic behind them is underspecified -> formalization shows many common rejections need not imply invalid IVs -> implementation guidance matters
framework: survey of current practice -> formal framework for negative controls in IV settings -> implementation guidance -> practical implications
innovation_source: the paper converts a loose empirical ritual into a formal design object with explicit assumptions and consequences
reusable_move: when an empirical practice is widespread but conceptually sloppy, the contribution can come from clarifying the object and showing current applications answer the wrong question

title: The Trade-Off between Flexibility and Robustness in Instrumental Variables Analysis
story_ladder: flexibility is usually discussed as a precision-versus-bias trade-off -> in IV there is another cost -> misspecification sensitivity rises with flexibility even in huge samples -> model choice is also a robustness choice
framework: model and motivation -> theoretical results -> implications for empirical practice -> calibrated illustration
innovation_source: the paper reframes functional-form choice in IV as a robustness design decision rather than only a convenience or sample-size issue
reusable_move: if a methodological choice is usually defended by realism, ask what hidden robustness cost realism imposes under approximate identification

title: Test-Optional Admissions
story_ladder: more information should improve selection -> colleges increasingly go test optional anyway -> social pressure makes information itself costly -> withholding scores becomes an institutional response rather than an information failure
framework: puzzle and motivation -> admissions model under social pressure -> test-optional regime and imputation rules -> extensions and implications
innovation_source: the contribution comes from treating admissions policy as a strategic information-management problem rather than a pure prediction problem
reusable_move: when institutions voluntarily discard information, look for external accountability or audience-pressure forces that make information politically expensive

title: Firm Responses and Wage Effects of Foreign Demand Shocks with Fixed Labor Costs and Monopsony
story_ladder: trade shocks affect firms directly and through networks -> firm responses reveal cost structure -> fixed labor costs and some monopsony matter -> aggregate wage incidence of tariffs is larger than benchmark models suggest
framework: data and motivating facts -> model and comparative statics -> identification strategy -> partial-equilibrium firm responses -> aggregate counterfactuals
innovation_source: the paper infers fixed versus variable labor cost structure from firm response elasticities and then uses that structure to revise aggregate wage incidence
reusable_move: micro response elasticities can be used not just as reduced-form facts but as diagnostics for hidden primitives that matter in general equilibrium

title: Keep Your Enemies Closer: Strategic Platform Adjustments during US and French Elections
story_ladder: median-voter convergence is foundational but hard to test directly -> campaign texts provide direct platform evidence -> quasirandom rival identity shifts reveal strategic moderation -> politicians visibly follow each other
framework: data and text measures -> reduced-form round-to-round convergence -> rival-identity RDD -> interpretation
innovation_source: the paper brings direct text-based evidence to a classic political-economy mechanism that is usually tested only indirectly
reusable_move: when a canonical theorem concerns latent strategy, build a new behavioral measure that observes the strategy itself rather than one noisy downstream outcome

title: Allocation Mechanisms with Mixture-Averse Preferences
story_ladder: many allocation mechanisms rely heavily on randomization -> that logic changes when people dislike mixtures -> efficiency sharply restricts lottery complexity -> standard mechanisms fail more often than expected
framework: baseline economy -> efficiency characterization -> identical-preference case -> implications for mechanism design and welfare
innovation_source: the paper turns a preference departure into a stark structural prediction about the shape of efficient allocations
reusable_move: when a preference modification is proposed, ask whether it yields a surprisingly simple characterization of efficient outcomes; that sharp prediction can carry the theory

title: Monopsony and Employer Misoptimization Explain Why Wages Bunch at Round Numbers
story_ladder: round-number bunching resembles familiar product-market pricing patterns -> test whether workers exhibit similar left-digit bias -> null evidence rejects the standard explanation -> the distortion lies on the employer side
framework: descriptive bunching fact -> experiments on labor supply around round numbers -> administrative replication -> employer-side explanation
innovation_source: the contribution comes from experimentally falsifying the obvious behavioral story and relocating the bias to firms rather than workers
reusable_move: when a stylized fact resembles a known phenomenon in another market, directly test the borrowed mechanism instead of assuming it transports

title: The Negligible Effect of Free Contraception on Fertility: Experimental Evidence from Burkina Faso
story_ladder: subsidized family planning is often treated as a central lever for fertility reduction -> test the claim directly in a high-fertility environment -> strong null rejects even modest effects -> the policy logic needs rethinking
framework: context and intervention -> experimental design -> fertility results -> complementary demand-friction interventions -> interpretation
innovation_source: the paper uses a high-powered trial to challenge one of the field's most cited policy assumptions, making the null itself the main contribution
reusable_move: a null result becomes field-shifting when the design is strong enough to reject the canonical policy magnitude, not merely fail to reject zero

title: Gender Differences in Economics Seminars
story_ladder: academic seminars are central to professional evaluation -> unequal treatment there can affect careers -> large-scale measurement reveals not just more questions for women but more disruptive and negative interruptions
framework: data and measurement -> interruption differentials -> tone and type analysis -> audience-composition channels -> interpretation
innovation_source: the paper turns a widely discussed professional friction into a measurable empirical object using both algorithmic and human coding
reusable_move: if a professional norm is often discussed anecdotally, combine scalable machine measurement with interpretable human coding to make the invisible visible

title: Optimal Taxation and Market Power
story_ladder: competition policy is the first-best response to market power -> taxation still matters when first-best tools are incomplete -> integrating oligopoly into optimal tax theory changes both qualitative and quantitative prescriptions
framework: model -> analytical tax formulas -> robustness and policy discussion -> quantitative calibration
innovation_source: the paper connects modern market-power concerns to canonical optimal-tax theory and decomposes the new tax logic into interpretable pieces
reusable_move: when extending a classic normative framework, give the reader a decomposition that names each new force separately; this makes the extension usable rather than merely more complex

title: Financial Frictions: Micro versus Macro Volatility
story_ladder: financial-frictions research focuses heavily on corporate spreads -> household credit spreads also move cyclically and matter for consumption -> integrating them into HANK changes both business-cycle and welfare conclusions
framework: empirical household evidence -> model with banks and households -> calibration -> aggregate and distributional implications
innovation_source: the paper shifts financial-frictions analysis from a firm-centered to a household-and-bank-spread-centered perspective
reusable_move: if a macro friction has mostly been studied on the firm side, ask whether the household-facing margin is equally cyclical and more distributionally important

title: The Price of War
story_ladder: the human cost of war is obvious, but the macro toll across countries is less systematically measured -> a long historical panel reveals large local and spillover effects -> trade and borders propagate the damage
framework: data and descriptive facts -> event-study dynamics -> causality discussion and restricted samples -> conclusion
innovation_source: the paper creates a macroeconomic map of war costs that includes noncombatant spillovers rather than focusing only on the war site
reusable_move: when studying a dramatic event, widen the unit of impact beyond the obvious directly hit location to the exposure network around it

title: A Theory of Supply Function Choice and Aggregate Supply
story_ladder: modern aggregate-supply theory implicitly assumes a restrictive firm strategy set -> allow richer supply choices -> the slope of aggregate supply becomes endogenous to the uncertainty environment -> long-run macro episodes look more interpretable
framework: model of supply-function choice -> equilibrium characterization -> implications for aggregate supply -> quantitative mapping to historical episodes
innovation_source: the paper revises a foundational macro object by changing the primitive strategic object firms choose
reusable_move: if a macro relation is treated as primitive, ask whether it is an equilibrium consequence of a deeper strategic choice that the literature has fixed by assumption

title: Cursed Sequential Equilibrium
story_ladder: cursed equilibrium is influential in static settings -> dynamic games need a sequential version -> extending cursedness changes canonical dynamic predictions -> experimental patterns support the new concept
framework: definition and properties of CSE -> applications to canonical games -> experimental relevance and comparison with other concepts
innovation_source: the contribution is to turn a well-known behavioral equilibrium idea into a dynamic solution concept with economically meaningful applications
reusable_move: to extend a canonical behavioral concept, show not only formal existence but also what breaks in classic applications once the extension is taken seriously

title: Monetary Cooperation during Global Inflation Surges
story_ladder: inflation is usually treated as something each central bank fights alone -> under global tradable scarcity some inflation helps reallocate supply -> spillovers mean each country underprovides that adjustment -> cooperation can reduce global contraction
framework: model and intuition -> cooperative versus noncooperative policy -> extensions to different scarcity origins -> discussion
innovation_source: the paper reframes inflation during global bottlenecks as partly a coordination problem rather than only a domestic stabilization problem
reusable_move: when a macro policy cost is local but part of the benefit is external, look for an underappreciated coordination failure even in domains usually framed as domestic policy

title: Anatomy of the Phillips Curve: Micro Evidence and Macro Implications
story_ladder: aggregate Phillips-curve estimates are small -> either pricing is inert or the wrong activity measure is being used -> micro evidence shows firms respond strongly to marginal cost -> the wedge lies between output and marginal cost, not between cost and price
framework: bottom-up estimation strategy -> micro pass-through results -> aggregation and reconciliation with macro evidence -> implications
innovation_source: the paper decomposes a famous macro puzzle into micro primitives and shows which link in the chain is actually weak
reusable_move: when a macro relation looks puzzling, break it into primitive elasticities and identify which component is truly small before theorizing broadly

title: Place-Based Redistribution
story_ladder: redistribution is usually discussed as place-blind -> migration and local markets mean taxation changes community composition -> optimal policy depends on why people sort where they do -> spatial redistribution has a rigorous tax basis
framework: model -> characterization of optimal location-specific taxes -> calibration and policy magnitudes -> sensitivity to migration responses
innovation_source: the paper imports Mirrleesian-style redistribution logic into a spatial equilibrium environment where place itself carries informational and general-equilibrium content
reusable_move: if a standard policy principle is spatially blind, ask whether location proxies for hidden traits strongly enough to overturn the blindness norm

title: Equal Pay for Similar Work
story_ladder: equal-pay rules seem straightforwardly fairness-improving -> firms can change job composition and assignment -> segregation becomes the adjustment margin -> intended equity policy can worsen group gaps
framework: model of EPSW policies -> equilibrium predictions -> empirical evaluation in Chile -> interpretation
innovation_source: the paper shows how a policy aimed at within-firm equity can backfire through endogenous task sorting and segregation
reusable_move: when policy regulates an outcome within categories, always ask whether agents can endogenously redraw the categories instead

title: Temporary Layoffs, Loss-of-Recall, and Cyclical Unemployment Dynamics
story_ladder: recalls make temporary layoffs look like a stabilizer -> data show many layoffs convert into nonrecall unemployment -> a model with loss-of-recall fits both historical and pandemic patterns -> policy that preserves recall margins matters a lot
framework: measurement of temporary-layoff flows -> structural model -> pre- and post-pandemic fit -> policy counterfactuals
innovation_source: the contribution is to elevate loss-of-recall from a background detail to a central cyclical mechanism
reusable_move: when an institutional category is treated as benign, inspect the transition out of that category; the hidden failure margin may drive the aggregate result

title: Diffusion of Reproductive Health Behavior through International Migration: Effects on Origin-Country Fertility
story_ladder: migration moves labor and income, but it may also move norms -> destination-country policy variation creates differential exposure across origin provinces -> fertility falls where migrant exposure to liberal policies is stronger -> migration becomes a channel of behavioral diffusion
framework: institutional background -> data construction -> shift-share policy-exposure design -> fertility results -> contraceptive mechanism analysis
innovation_source: the paper identifies the content of transmitted norms by tying migration networks to specific policy changes in destination countries rather than only to migrant flows
reusable_move: when studying norm transmission, interact migration exposure with policy content abroad so the diffusion channel has interpretable substance rather than generic contact

title: A Preferred-Habitat Model of Term Premia, Exchange Rates, and Monetary Policy Spillovers
story_ladder: standard open-economy models imply strong insulation under floating rates -> empirical bond, FX, and QE evidence contradicts that -> segmented clienteles and limited arbitrage restore the missing spillovers
framework: model -> equilibrium implications without and with demand risk -> estimation and fit -> policy transmission
innovation_source: the paper creates a unified asset-pricing explanation for multiple international-finance anomalies and policy spillovers
reusable_move: if several anomalies live in adjacent markets, build one mechanism that explains their coexistence rather than treating them as separate puzzles

title: Do Credit Conditions Move House Prices?
story_ladder: existing studies reach opposite conclusions about credit and housing -> the hidden difference is the degree of market segmentation -> estimating that margin reconciles the debate
framework: supply-demand intuition -> empirical estimation using credit instruments -> flexible housing model -> quantitative decomposition
innovation_source: the contribution is to identify the sufficient statistic that nests the literature's polar cases and calibrates the relevant middle ground
reusable_move: when a literature is split by polar modeling assumptions, identify the one elasticity or margin that spans the spectrum and measure it directly

title: Work from Home and the Office Real Estate Apocalypse
story_ladder: remote work visibly empties offices -> the real question is what that means for asset values, banks, and city finances -> lease data plus valuation modeling reveal large, persistent destruction
framework: office-market evidence -> valuation model -> city and national calibrations -> implications for financial and fiscal fragility
innovation_source: the paper turns a social shift in work organization into a quantified asset-pricing and urban-finance shock
reusable_move: when a new social practice changes demand for a long-lived asset, combine current cash-flow evidence with a transition valuation model rather than waiting for transactions alone

title: A Long and a Short Leg Make for a Wobbly Equilibrium
story_ladder: short sellers should attack larger mispricing -> in practice activity can collapse abruptly -> the missing piece is the lending market and equilibrium feedback in borrow fees
framework: model -> equilibrium multiplicity condition -> empirical patterns in short activity -> interpretation
innovation_source: the paper transforms stock lending from a background friction into the central state variable generating instability in short-selling
reusable_move: if a market behavior looks unstable, inspect the complementary market that enables the behavior; instability may live there rather than in the visible market itself

title: The Value of Software
story_ladder: software became a dominant asset in the digital economy -> if markets were fully rational this revaluation should be quick -> long-lived anomalies suggest investors learn far more slowly than standard models imply
framework: rise of software in equity markets -> forecast and return anomalies -> gradual-learning interpretation -> implications
innovation_source: the paper prices a modern intangible asset by treating its rise as a long information-processing failure rather than an immediate repricing event
reusable_move: when a new technology rises gradually, ask whether the main puzzle is not the technology itself but the market's speed of learning about it

title: Supply, Demand, Institutions, and Firms: A Theory of Labor Market Sorting and the Wage Distribution
story_ladder: labor economics often treats supply-demand and firm heterogeneity as separate traditions -> wage inequality reflects both simultaneously -> a unified model changes which shocks look important
framework: unified theory -> estimation on Brazilian data -> decomposition of wage-distribution changes -> interaction effects
innovation_source: the paper merges two literatures that usually talk past each other and shows their interaction is quantitatively first order
reusable_move: if two literatures explain the same outcome with different primitives, the idea is often to make them interact rather than choose one winner

title: Consumer Credit and the Incidence of Tariffs: Evidence from the Auto Industry
story_ladder: tariff incidence is usually measured in product prices -> many purchases are financed -> vertically linked lenders create another pass-through channel -> total consumer burden is larger and more unequal
framework: institutional background on captive finance -> empirical design -> heterogeneous incidence -> interpretation
innovation_source: the paper identifies consumer credit as a hidden tariff-incidence margin in durable-goods markets
reusable_move: when a product is commonly financed, incidence analysis that ignores credit terms is probably incomplete

title: Market-Wide Predictable Price Pressure
story_ladder: standard finance assumes aggregate markets absorb uninformed flows without moving price -> scheduled cash distributions provide advance-known flow shocks -> prices still move when the trades happen -> market-level price pressure is real
framework: predictable flow construction -> return forecasting evidence -> cross-market and mechanism variation -> interpretation
innovation_source: the paper demonstrates that price pressure is not a small-stock anomaly but a market-wide force in the most liquid assets
reusable_move: the cleanest test of flow-driven price impact uses trades whose timing and size are known in advance, stripping away private-information stories

title: Power Flows: Transmission Lines, Allocative Efficiency, and Corporate Profits
story_ladder: transmission is usually discussed as an efficiency and decarbonization issue -> incomplete integration also creates concentrated corporate winners from the status quo -> political economy becomes central to why reform is slow
framework: background and data -> inefficiency calculations -> sources of spatial constraints -> firm-level winners and losers
innovation_source: the paper integrates allocative efficiency with political economy by quantifying both aggregate gains and incumbent losses
reusable_move: if a reform is obviously efficient yet blocked, quantify the concentrated private losses of incumbents alongside the diffuse social gains

title: The Long-Term Effects of Income for At-Risk Infants: Evidence from Supplemental Security Income
story_ladder: early-life cash transfers often show long-run benefits -> this program provides a much larger and more targeted intervention -> strong first stage still yields null outcome effects -> not all disadvantaged early-life conditions are equally remediable through cash
framework: policy background -> data linkage -> first-stage transfer effects -> short-run health outcomes -> long-run educational and labor outcomes
innovation_source: the paper uses an unusually rich administrative linkage to test a powerful early-income intervention on an especially vulnerable infant population
reusable_move: if prior evidence suggests a broad positive effect of a policy class, test its limits in the most extreme or policy-relevant margin rather than assuming monotonic gains

title: Downward Rigidity in the Wage for New Hires
story_ladder: wage rigidity matters for macro but evidence on new hires is limited -> vacancy-posted wages offer a direct measure -> job-level evidence reveals asymmetric rigidity
framework: data and measure of new-hire wages -> frequency and direction of wage changes -> cyclical responsiveness -> interpretation
innovation_source: the paper finds the right micro object for new-hire wages and shows that aggregation had hidden the relevant rigidity
reusable_move: if a macro debate lacks clean evidence, search for the exact micro object the theory refers to instead of using a broad average as a proxy

title: Across-Country Wage Compression in Multinationals
story_ladder: wages are usually treated as locally determined -> multinationals may instead coordinate compensation globally -> headquarters shocks show up in foreign workers' pay -> internal norms matter across borders
framework: multinational structure and data -> headquarters-shock identification -> foreign wage transmission -> interpretation of wage anchoring
innovation_source: the paper identifies a firm-internal wage-setting channel that compresses cross-country wage differences beyond local-market fundamentals
reusable_move: if a firm spans many markets, look for headquarters-origin shocks to test whether decisions are truly local or centrally anchored

title: Strategic Voting in Two-Party Legislative Elections
story_ladder: multidistrict elections aggregate preferences differently than single-district contests -> strategic voting across dimensions changes what policies survive -> legislative competition can improve aggregation properties
framework: model -> strategic voting characterization -> candidate behavior -> policy properties and comparisons
innovation_source: the paper shows how legislative structure can discipline multidimensional policy choice through strategic voter attention
reusable_move: when political aggregation seems messy, ask whether the institutional setting changes which dimension voters strategically emphasize

title: What You Don’t Know May Be Good for You
story_ladder: transparency is usually treated as beneficial -> experts respond strategically to public performance data -> risky clients get avoided -> information can worsen matching even while helping clients screen
framework: model of experts and clients -> equilibrium with and without public information -> welfare comparison
innovation_source: the contribution is to expose the reputational selection effect that can reverse the standard case for report cards
reusable_move: when evaluating transparency, always ask how the measured side of the market changes its selection behavior in response

title: Robustness Measures for Welfare Analysis
story_ladder: welfare analysis routinely leans on demand assumptions -> debates about realism are often qualitative -> robustness measures convert that debate into a quantitative margin
framework: welfare problem under functional-form uncertainty -> robustness metrics -> computation and applications
innovation_source: the paper builds a portable diagnostic that can travel with welfare estimates instead of replacing them
reusable_move: when a result depends on a hard-to-defend assumption, do not only vary assumptions; quantify how far reality must move before the conclusion breaks

title: Intermediated Asymmetric Information, Compensation, and Career Prospects
story_ladder: intermediaries appear to add value by identifying talent -> that same informational edge allows them to exploit agents -> dynamic churning and compensation reflect the race between reputation formation and information rent extraction
framework: model of agents, intermediary, and outside market -> equilibrium compensation dynamics -> churn and career implications
innovation_source: the paper treats career paths as shaped by informational intermediation rather than only by search or matching frictions
reusable_move: if an intermediary solves an information problem, ask how that advantage can also be used to extract rents from the very agents it helps place

title: Moonshot: Public R&D and Growth
story_ladder: the moonshot is the iconic example of transformative public R&D -> credible evidence has been lacking -> new identification shows real but modest growth effects -> symbolism exceeds aggregate measured payoff
framework: historical context and data -> identification strategy -> local and national effects -> mechanism and interpretation
innovation_source: the paper reevaluates a legendary policy using modern causal tools, producing a disciplined estimate rather than a celebratory narrative
reusable_move: high-profile historical programs are ideal for contribution when the mythology is strong but the causal evidence is weak

title: Racial Disparities in Housing Returns
story_ladder: low minority housing returns are often attributed to lower appreciation -> the bigger force is distress -> homeownership as a wealth-building tool fails through a financial-fragility channel
framework: return measurement -> distress decomposition -> determinants of distress -> policy implications
innovation_source: the paper shifts the explanation for racial return gaps from price appreciation to realized exit conditions under financial stress
reusable_move: when a return gap exists, decompose entry, holding, and exit margins before concluding that the asset itself appreciates differently

title: Abundance from Abroad: Migrant Income and Long-Run Economic Development
story_ladder: migration is often studied as remittance support -> bigger question is whether foreign earnings prospects rewire local development trajectories -> crisis-driven shocks show large long-run domestic spillovers
framework: identification using exchange-rate shocks -> long-run reduced-form effects -> structural decomposition of mechanisms
innovation_source: the paper treats migrant income as a development shock to the origin economy, not just a household transfer
reusable_move: if an international shock enters households directly, ask whether its main long-run effect is actually on the domestic economy through endogenous local adjustment

title: Micro versus Macro Labor Supply Elasticities: The Role of Dynamic Returns to Effort
story_ladder: micro and macro labor-supply elasticities often conflict -> top careers feature dynamic returns and discrete pay adjustments -> job-switch-based evidence closes part of the gap
framework: model of dynamic compensation -> descriptive life-cycle evidence -> tax-reform quasi-experiment focused on switchers -> macro interpretation
innovation_source: the paper transforms job switching from a nuisance into the key empirical window on long-run labor-supply behavior
reusable_move: when short-run quasi-experimental estimates seem too small for macro use, look for the career margin through which incentives translate with delay

title: Innovative Ideas and Gender (In)Equality
story_ladder: historical examples of women losing credit motivate a modern question -> ordinary citation counts are inadequate because relevance is endogenous -> text similarity creates a counterfactual citation benchmark -> omission rates reveal who gets underrecognized
framework: data construction -> similarity and omission measure -> empirical gap estimates -> heterogeneity -> discussion of discrimination and policy implications
innovation_source: the paper turns a soft and usually anecdotal concept, idea omission, into a measurable empirical object
reusable_move: if recognition is hard to observe directly, construct a counterfactual benchmark for who should have been acknowledged and study deviations from that benchmark

title: Imperfect Competition and Rents in Labor and Product Markets: The Case of the Construction Industry
story_ladder: existing work measures labor or product power separately -> firms often exercise both at once -> procurement data reveal both margins -> the interaction changes welfare and incidence
framework: joint model -> implications of double market power -> data and identification -> quantification of rents and incidence
innovation_source: the paper fuses monopsony and markup literatures inside one institution where rich bidding data help identify both objects
reusable_move: when two literatures explain the same outcome with different primitives, estimate them jointly instead of choosing one winner

title: Employers and Unemployment Insurance Take-Up
story_ladder: employers matter in labor markets beyond wages -> UI agencies actively involve employers in take-up decisions -> organizational behavior becomes a major determinant of program access and progressivity
framework: institutional background -> claim and appeal rates -> employer-effects decomposition -> wage-gradient interpretation -> policy implications
innovation_source: the contribution is to treat the employer as a gatekeeper to social insurance rather than a background institution
reusable_move: when program take-up is incomplete, decompose access into individual frictions and organizational gatekeeping effects

title: Direct and Indirect Effects of Investment Tax Incentives
story_ladder: standard policy evaluation asks whether treated firms invest more -> the broader question is whether local production systems expand or are merely reshuffled -> spillover mapping changes the policy assessment
framework: policy background -> direct effects -> geographic and industry spillovers -> decomposition of channels
innovation_source: the paper identifies positive and negative general-equilibrium spillovers in one design rather than stopping at firm-level treatment effects
reusable_move: if a place-based or firm-targeted policy likely changes local equilibrium, trace effects through supplier, demand, and competitor networks before judging it

title: Underbidding for Oil and Gas Tracts
story_ladder: common-values theory imposes sharp equilibrium restrictions when ex post value is observable -> those restrictions can be tested directly -> the data point toward underbidding
framework: framework -> falsifiable implications -> data -> participation test -> underbidding evidence
innovation_source: the paper uses equilibrium tests as a first-pass diagnostic before imposing stronger structural assumptions
reusable_move: if theory yields observable inequalities or independence implications, test those first instead of jumping straight to a full structural model

title: A Goldilocks Theory of Fiscal Deficits
story_ladder: the textbook view says larger deficits eventually explode debt -> low rates and the ZLB complicate that simple monotonic story -> fiscal space is state dependent and nonmonotone
framework: model -> fiscal space outside the ZLB -> fiscal space near the ZLB -> calibration and comparative statics
innovation_source: the paper reframes deficit debates around a narrow and parameterized Goldilocks region rather than a binary pro- or anti-deficit stance
reusable_move: when policy debates are binary, look for the latent state variable that turns the answer into a region rather than a slogan

title: Raising the Stakes: Physician Facility Investments and Provider Agency
story_ladder: principal-agent problems in medicine are usually framed as overprovision of procedures -> the location of treatment is another important margin -> ownership creates a sharp incentive change that reveals the preexisting distortion
framework: market background -> ownership and regulatory setting -> data -> empirical strategy -> spending and behavior effects
innovation_source: the paper uses entrepreneurial investment as a lens to measure provider agency in treatment-setting choice
reusable_move: when agents choose both what to do and where to do it, exploit shocks to the location incentive to reveal hidden agency distortions

title: Treatment Effects in Market Equilibrium
story_ladder: standard experiments assume limited interference -> many policy settings are markets where interference is the point -> market equilibrium must enter the treatment-effect object itself
framework: model and estimands -> estimation and inference -> heterogeneous treatment effects and targeting -> application logic
innovation_source: the paper builds a bridge between experimental design and equilibrium policy evaluation
reusable_move: if treatment changes prices or allocation rules, redesign the experiment to recover the market elasticities needed for policy interpretation

title: International Trade Responses to Labor Market Regulations
story_ladder: trade models often separate domestic labor regulation from international competitiveness -> posted-worker markets place them side by side -> regulatory reforms become trade shocks
framework: institutional setting -> measurement of service trade and labor costs -> gravity model -> reform-based interpretation
innovation_source: the paper turns labor-market regulation into a first-order determinant of cross-border trade in services
reusable_move: if a policy directly changes delivered marginal cost in a traded activity, treat it as a trade policy whether or not it is labeled that way

title: Managers and Public Hospital Performance
story_ladder: public-service performance is often attributed to budgets or workers at the front line -> top management may be a binding constraint -> a recruitment reform provides causal leverage
framework: setting and reform -> reduced-form impact on mortality -> evidence that managers matter -> quality-composition channel
innovation_source: the paper ties an administrative reform to a clean manager-quality margin rather than treating management as a vague residual
reusable_move: when an institution changes who gets hired, use it to separate management quality from general reform effects

title: Making Bricks from Straw: Resources and Productivity in Health Care
story_ladder: weak public-service performance is often blamed on effort or governance -> unrestricted money reveals what workers do when the resource margin is loosened -> behavior points to capital scarcity as a major constraint
framework: context and experiment -> rollout and survey data -> productivity effects -> spending and motivation mechanisms
innovation_source: the paper opens the black box of grant use with unusually rich expenditure and text data
reusable_move: if an organization looks dysfunctional, give it flexible resources and study how it self-identifies its bottlenecks

title: Risk Preferences and Field Behavior: The Relevance of Higher-Order Risk Preferences
story_ladder: the literature often fails to link laboratory risk aversion to field behavior -> perhaps it measures the wrong preference object -> higher-order preferences recover the missing predictive power
framework: experimental design -> methods for measuring higher-order preferences -> determinants -> links to field behavior
innovation_source: the paper operationalizes higher-order risk preferences at scale and shows their empirical relevance outside the lab
reusable_move: when a classic trait seems weak, measure the higher-order version that the theoretical mechanism actually requires

title: Is Air Pollution Regulation Too Lenient? Evidence from US Offset Markets
story_ladder: cost-benefit debates usually struggle on the cost side -> offset markets reveal actual willingness to pay for abatement -> matching those prices to benefits gives a policy-stringency test
framework: history and design of offset markets -> data -> descriptive price patterns -> efficiency comparison -> implications and extensions
innovation_source: the paper turns a decentralized environmental market into a sufficient statistic for regulatory stringency
reusable_move: if a policy creates a shadow market for compliance, use its prices to infer marginal costs instead of relying only on engineering estimates

title: Monotonicity among Judges: Evidence from Judicial Panels and Consequences for Judge IV Designs
story_ladder: monotonicity is central but usually unobservable -> panel decisions make it observable -> direct evidence replaces speculation and clarifies how much the practical bias matters
framework: theory of judge monotonicity -> data and settings -> measurement of violations -> consequences for IV -> checks on panel-specific effects
innovation_source: the paper measures a key identification assumption directly rather than asking indirect proxy tests to do impossible work
reusable_move: search for institutional settings where an abstract identifying assumption becomes literally observable

title: A Model of Populism as a Conspiracy Theory
story_ladder: populism combines anti-elite rhetoric, conspiratorial framing, and reduced accountability -> a model of alternative reality formation can explain that package coherently
framework: model setup -> equilibrium logic -> implications for accountability and policy choice -> discussion of observed populist behavior
innovation_source: the paper models political strategy as the manipulation of voters' interpretive frame rather than just policy promises
reusable_move: when a political phenomenon looks irrational, ask whether actors are first changing how evidence is interpreted rather than changing the evidence itself

title: Immigration, Innovation, and Growth
story_ladder: immigration debates stay stuck because migrants self-select into growing places -> a new instrument isolates exogenous local shocks -> dynamic innovation effects change the welfare calculus
framework: data -> instrument construction -> reduced-form innovation and wage effects -> wage-inequality results -> structural interpretation
innovation_source: the paper pairs a new immigration instrument with a growth framework that accumulates medium-run gains
reusable_move: when a policy or shock likely changes innovation, do not stop at short-run labor-market outcomes; trace the dynamic margin too

title: Evaluating the Impact of Urban Transit Infrastructure: Evidence from Bogotá’s TransMilenio
story_ladder: transit projects are often evaluated by engineering time savings -> cities are spatial equilibria -> the true gains and their distribution depend on reallocation and land-use responses
framework: background and data -> quantitative city model -> reduced-form elasticities and sufficient statistics -> welfare and distributional counterfactuals
innovation_source: the paper bridges a sufficient-statistics approach and a richer structural urban model in one application
reusable_move: compare the naive engineering object to the equilibrium welfare object to show exactly what the standard metric misses

title: Market Power and Capital Constraints
story_ladder: intermediary-asset-pricing papers emphasize capital constraints while market-microstructure papers emphasize market power -> real-world auctions involve both -> their interaction changes prices and liquidity
framework: model -> quantification and identification of shadow costs -> policy interpretation
innovation_source: the paper unifies two usually separate financial frictions inside a tractable auction environment
reusable_move: when two literatures hold different frictions fixed, the best contribution may be to let both vary in the same institution

title: Nested Bundling
story_ladder: firms commonly sell nested plans but theory gives little clean guidance -> a simple partial order recovers when that common practice is actually optimal
framework: model -> main results and converse -> proof sketch -> discussion and examples
innovation_source: the paper translates an intractable multidimensional mechanism-design problem into a tractable order-and-algorithm characterization
reusable_move: if a business practice is ubiquitous but theory is messy, search for the monotone order that rationalizes the practice

title: Games on Multiplex Networks
story_ladder: real social systems are multilayer but most network games are not -> adding layers changes both equilibrium and targeting -> multilayer complexity is therefore not decorative but substantive
framework: model and applications -> equilibrium characterization -> policy implications and simulations -> extensions
innovation_source: the paper provides a tractable framework for multiplex network games that remains usable for policy analysis
reusable_move: when agents split scarce attention or resources across contexts, treat those contexts as interacting layers rather than collapsing them into one average network
